neighbours.label: interjection punctuation in old-fashioned literary dialogue ('Oh!', 'Why,', 'But--'); weak and unclear
fire: "You walked all the way from the village in this weather? Oh! You must be frozen through," said the housekeeper.
"Why, if it isn't young Master Thomas come home at last!" cried the old servant at the gate.
"I would have gone with him. But--would you credit it?--he left before dawn without a word."
"Oh! How very kind of you to call, and on such a dreary afternoon," said Mrs. Pemberton.
"Why, the creature understands every word we say!" exclaimed the parson, laughing.
"We might as well try to stop the tide with a broom," grumbled the old sailor by the fire.
"She promised to write. But--alas!--not a single letter came all that winter."
"Oh! Do not speak of it, sir; the very thought makes me tremble," replied the young lady.
